exposure: maternal normal stature (height between 10th and 90th centiles)
outcome: cesarean delivery (CD) due to cephalopelvic disproportion (CPD)
cohort: The study included 3295 women with singleton deliveries who experienced adverse obstetric outcomes related to labor dystocia at a single tertiary center between 2014-2020.
finding: Among women experiencing adverse obstetric outcomes related to labor dystocia, specifically those undergoing cesarean delivery due to cephalopelvic disproportion, short stature and nulliparity were independently associated with decreased neonatal birth weight.
mod_finding: Among women with short stature, cesarean delivery due to cephalopelvic disproportion occurs at lower neonatal birth weights (3215 ± 411 g) compared to normal stature women (3484 ± 427 g).
birth_weight: Babies included had varying birth weights, with mean birth weights of 3215 ± 411 g for the short stature group and 3484 ± 427 g for the normal stature group in cases of CD due to CPD.
